handoff: Changes requested, 1 blocking: worktreesDir builds on an unresolved norn home but is prefix-matched against resolved git worktree paths, so a symlinked home breaks tidy's orphan check and marker inference (paths.ts:130). All 16 criteria traced; test+typecheck green.

findings.title: worktreesDir uses an unresolved home but is prefix-matched against resolved git worktree paths
findings.detail:
`worktreesDir(root) = join(machineDir(root), 'worktrees')`. machineDir comes from `machineHomeOf(root)` = the bound home or `nornHome()` (paths.ts:124, 231), and neither runs realpath. Context resolves the repo root (context.ts:62 'main checkout (realpath)') because paths from git are canonical, and the harness resolves its temp dir (harness.ts:348) for the same reason. Three places now compare paths that git reports (resolved) with `${worktreesDir(root)}/` by string prefix: observe's orphan check (packages/cli/src/runtime/observe/index.ts:176) and `inferUnitMarker` (packages/store/src/worktree.ts:91), which is called from classifyWorktrees on every tick. When the home is reached through a symlink (`~/.norn -> ~/dotfiles/norn`, or `NORN_HOME_DIR=/tmp/h` on macOS where /tmp -> /private/tmp), decide creates worktrees at `/tmp/h/repos/<id>/worktrees/...`, but git lists them as `/private/tmp/h/...`. Then (a) `norn tidy` and the tick's orphans never see orphan worktrees (breaks user story 7: tidy reports and removes orphan worktrees in the machine dir's worktrees/), and (b) a unit worktree whose `.norn-unit` marker `git clean -fdx` removed is no longer inferred and restored, so the unit loses its worktree. Before this change both checks used `${root}-worktrees` with root resolved, so this failure is new. The plan's Risks section names it ('the realpath of the home ... a worktree path compared against git worktree list output may differ in spelling'). No test covers it: every harness home sits under a resolved dir. Not reproduced live in this session (the hook refuses `git worktree add` from the shell). The reasoning rests on git recording a worktree's resolved path, which is the /var vs /private/var mismatch the handoff's Easy to miss already notes.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Resolve the home once where it is chosen: realpath it (e.g. the existing `realOr`) in `bindNornHome` and in `machineHomeOf`'s fallback, or in `worktreesDir`. Then add an integration test in worktrees-machine-dir.test.ts that binds the home through a symlink (the command's home given as a symlink to a real folder) and checks that a tidy orphan is still reported, and that a story worktree with its marker deleted is still inferred.

findings.title: Default decide fixture still reports the old `/r-worktrees` folder
findings.detail:
The shared Facts fixture sets `repo.worktrees: '/r-worktrees'`, the layout this story removes. Every decide test except the two new ones in decide.test.ts therefore keeps building paths beside the repo root. This is harmless, because decide is path-agnostic and the new tests pin the folder, but it is misleading to a reader.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Point the fixture at a machine-dir-shaped folder (e.g. `/home/.norn/repos/r-00000000/worktrees`) when the fixture is next touched.
